title: Mexican Cooperation Agency Opens Its First Overseas Branch in Havana
author: Sputnik
content:
_This article by[Sputnik](https://www.jornada.com.mx/) originally appeared in
the [November 21, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/21/politica/agencia-
mexicana-de-cooperacion-abrio-en-la-habana-su-primera-filial-en-el-exterior),
Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Havana.** The **Mexican Agency for International Development Cooperation
(Amexcid)** inaugurated its first overseas branch in Cuba to facilitate
collaboration between the two peoples and jointly develop solutions to common
challenges, Executive Director Alejandra del Moral reported yesterday.

> “Today we open a new door in international cooperation that is full of
> opportunities for all peoples, for our peoples.”
>
> Alejandra del Moral, Executive Director of Amexcid

She stressed the symbolic importance of this office in Havana, given the
historic ties of friendship and fraternity between the two countries and
Mexico’s respect for the island’s cultural wealth and its “commitment to
dignity and resistance.” “This is where we will have an open door to dialogue,
understanding and the exchange of knowledge, so that we can build joint
solutions to common challenges,” she emphasized.

At the office’s inauguration, Cuban Deputy Prime Minister Óscar Pérez-Oliva
Fraga emphasized that **more than 25,000 producers** in his country benefit
from funding, supplies and training provided by Mexico “to grow food for our
country at a time of an intensified blockade,” referring to the economic
sanctions imposed by the United States.

Amexcid is an agency responsible for coordinating, planning and carrying out
Mexico’s international cooperation policies, with a global reach that
prioritizes sustainable development and integration in Latin America and the
Caribbean, as both a provider and recipient of technical, financial and
academic assistance and under the principle of shared responsibility.

Meanwhile, US Democratic Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib said Donald Trump’s
administration “is suffocating the Cuban people. Our new Democratic majority
must act immediately to end Trump’s fuel blockade, prevent any military action
and, finally, end the embargo that has inflicted economic warfare on Cuba for
more than half a century,” she wrote on her X account.
